positions.as_written: Assess the hip when the lateral knee is painful, because the band crosses both joints and tension at one end is felt at the other.
Expect the band to contribute to rotational control as well as to coronal stability.
Preserve the capsulo-osseous layer where an approach allows it, since it carries the rotational restraint the superficial layer does not.
Identify Gerdy's tubercle before any anterolateral work.
Treat the band as the main passive restraint to internal rotation at the knee, with the anterolateral ligament and the capsule contributing.
Consider the band's deep layers rather than its surface when a rotational problem is being addressed.
Assess hip abductor function in a knee with lateral symptoms, because the band's tension is set above the knee.
Plan any lateral extra-articular procedure around the capsulo-osseous layer and the Kaplan fibres, which 2.11.2 covers, and 7.30 carries the technique.
